note: Hemophilia B dogs (with mice and monkeys) were relied on for both modalities: albumin-fused and subcutaneous FIX proteins, and liver-directed AAV FIX-Padua; their predictions held for every member with a scored comparison.
label: Hemophilia B (FIX)

engagement.population: Severe or moderately severe hemophilia B (FIX activity ≤2%)
engagement.model: Rats, rabbits and FIX-knockout mice dosed with rIX-FP (albumin-fused FIX)
engagement.note: Albumin fusion raised FIX recovery, terminal half-life and AUC in rats, rabbits and FIX-null mice.
engagement.short: Albumin fusion extends FIX half-life in rodents
engagement.quote: Furthermore, in-vivo recovery, terminal half-life and the AUC of rIX-FPs in rats and rabbits as determined by FIX antigen measurements were significantly increased compared to rFIX (BeneFIX).

engagement.magnitude_basis: fold prolongation of FIX persistence vs comparator FIX: dogs ~3.2× (antigen >0.05 IU/mL, 7.3 vs 2.3 days), patients >5× (half-life)
engagement.population: Severe or moderately severe hemophilia B (FIX activity ≤2%)
engagement.confidence_note: Both abstracts only. Dog metric (time above 5%) differs from the human one (terminal half-life).
engagement.model: Hemophilia B dogs and cynomolgus monkeys dosed with rIX-FP
engagement.note: Dogs held FIX above 5% about 3× longer on rIX-FP; in patients its half-life was 92 h, over 5× their previous FIX.
engagement.quote: In the 50-IU/kg cohort (13 subjects), the mean half-life of rIX-FP was 92 hours, more than 5 times longer than the subjects' previous FIX product.
engagement.judgement: Paired by me: Nolte 2012 states the dog/monkey PK and that 'Clinical studies will test whether the improved kinetics result in a significant half-life extension in patients'; Santagostino 2012 (same month) reports it. Phase 1 registry record not looked up.

engagement.population: Severe or moderately severe hemophilia B (FIX activity ≤2%)
engagement.confidence_note: Full text (PMC6029626); cited preclinical refs are Crudele 2015 (dogs) and Simioni 2009.
engagement.model: Hemophilia B dogs given liver-directed AAV8-canine FIX-Padua (R338L)
engagement.note: Patients given SPK-9001 (fidanacogene) expressed FIX-Padua with the 8-12× specific activity dogs had shown; mean steady-state FIX 33.7%.
engagement.quote: Furthermore, transgene-derived factor IX–specific activity was consistent with results from preclinical studies.
engagement.judgement: Kept the cell at same although BAX 335 (AskBio009) lost expression in 7 of 8 patients by 5-11 weeks (Konkle 2021, epub 2020) after FIX-null mice at 4e11 vg/kg held >50% FIX for 42 weeks (Monahan 2015): that is a different model (mouse) and the status is the best model's; Konkle states 'animal models of liver-directed AAV gene therapy do not predict or reproduce the cell-mediated immune response directed against AAV'. model_change true: a dog FIX-Padua model replaces the rIX-FP PK model and the comparison is now stated.

dose.population: Severe or moderately severe hemophilia B (FIX activity ≤2%)
dose.model: Hemophilia B dogs and cynomolgus monkeys dosed with rIX-FP
dose.note: Single 50-500 IU/kg rIX-FP doses kept aPTT below 60 s about 4× longer than rFIX in hemophilia B dogs.
dose.quote: Prolonged PDs of rIX-FP were demonstrated with APTT<60 s sustained around four times longer with rIX-FP (5.9 days) than rFIX (1.5 days).

dose.magnitude_basis: dosing interval supported (dog aPTT <60 s for 5.9 days vs human weekly trough 20%)
dose.population: Severe or moderately severe hemophilia B (FIX activity ≤2%)
dose.confidence_note: Patient side full text; dog side abstract only. The dogs gave no explicit human regimen target, so this is direction only.
dose.model: Hemophilia B dogs and cynomolgus monkeys dosed with rIX-FP
dose.note: Weekly 40 IU/kg kept a mean FIX trough of 20 IU/dL in patients, and every-2-week 75 IU/kg 12 IU/dL; prophylaxis worked.
dose.quote: Patients maintained a mean trough of 20 and 12 IU/dL FIX activity on prophylaxis with rIX-FP 40 IU/kg weekly and 75 IU/kg every 2 weeks, respectively.
dose.reason: Weekly regimen reached target in patients
dose.judgement: Paired by me; the dose rule row 'reached, drug worked' applies (primary AsBR endpoint met). Registry date is NCT01496274's results posting (marked ESTIMATED in the API).

dose.population: Severe or moderately severe hemophilia B (FIX activity ≤2%)
dose.model: Hemophilia B dogs given liver-directed AAV8-canine FIX-Padua (R338L)
dose.note: AAV8 FIX-Padua at 1-3×10¹² vg/kg gave hemophilia B dogs 25-40% FIX activity with 8-12× specific activity.
dose.quote: Two naïve HB dogs showed sustained expression of FIX-Padua with an 8- to 12-fold increased specific activity reaching 25% to 40% activity without antibody formation to FIX.

dose.magnitude_basis: FIX activity reached; vector doses not comparable across capsids (dog AAV8 vs human AAV-Spark100)
dose.population: Severe or moderately severe hemophilia B (FIX activity ≤2%)
dose.confidence_note: Patient side full text; dog side abstract.
dose.model: Hemophilia B dogs given liver-directed AAV8-canine FIX-Padua (R338L)
dose.note: At 5×10¹¹ vg/kg SPK-9001 gave a mean steady-state FIX of 33.7%, within the dogs' 25-40%, ending prophylaxis.
dose.quote: Vector-derived factor IX coagulant activity was sustained in all the participants, with a mean (±SD) steady-state factor IX coagulant activity of 33.7±18.5% (range, 14 to 81).
dose.reason: Target FIX level reached in patients
dose.judgement: Paired: George 2017 cites Crudele 2015 but the stated agreement is about specific activity (engagement), not the dose. Patients reached the dogs' FIX range at a lower vector dose on a different capsid, so magnitude is direction only. Not scored: FDA's NHP toxicology (2-10× the clinical dose, no test-article findings; SBRA 2024) as a decision-16 margin, because patients reached the dose but 62% needed glucocorticoids for transaminase rises, so 'dosed without that toxicity' does not cleanly hold.

efficacy.population: Severe or moderately severe hemophilia B (FIX activity ≤2%)
efficacy.note: rIX-FP reduced tail-tip bleeding time in FIX-null mice.
efficacy.short: rIX-FP cut bleeding in FIX-null mice
efficacy.quote: The efficacy in reducing bleeding time was shown in FIX(-/-) mice by a tail tip bleeding model.

efficacy.population: Severe or moderately severe hemophilia B (FIX activity ≤2%)
efficacy.confidence_note: Mouse side abstract only; it tested acute bleeding, not prophylaxis.
efficacy.note: Primary endpoint met: median spontaneous bleeding rate fell 100% when patients moved from on-demand to weekly rIX-FP prophylaxis.
efficacy.quote: There was 100% reduction in median annualized spontaneous bleeding rate (AsBR) and 100% resolution of target joints when subjects switched from on-demand to prophylaxis treatment with rIX-FP (P< .0001).
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me; Santagostino 2016 cites preclinical PK/PD only in general terms.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: steady-state FIX activity (dogs: to normal at 300 IU/kg; patients: mild range at 100 IU/kg)
efficacy.population: Severe or moderately severe hemophilia B (FIX activity ≤2%)
efficacy.confidence_note: Both full text (PMC8359950, PMC7592742). Dog paper published Oct 2020 but describes the work that enabled the Phase 1/2 study.
efficacy.model: Hemophilia B dogs given subcutaneous dalcinonacog alfa
efficacy.note: Dogs on daily SC dosing reached a correcting steady state; all patients on daily SC 100 IU/kg reached FIX ≥12%, the primary endpoint.
efficacy.short: SC FIX reached ≥12%, as dogs predicted
efficacy.quote: The primary efficacy endpoint in this study was met.
efficacy.judgement: The Phase 2b primary endpoint is a FIX level, so it governs efficacy even though it reads like exposure. Dog quote: 'reaching a steady-state activity sufficient to correct severe hemophilia to normal, after four days'. Not a retrodiction: the dog work preceded the clinic ('facilitated the initiation ... of the Phase 1/2 subcutaneous dosing study'). model_change: dog SC model replaces the mouse bleeding model.

efficacy.population: Severe or moderately severe hemophilia B (FIX activity ≤2%)
efficacy.confidence_note: SBRA full text; Cuker 2024 NEJM (10.1056/NEJMoa2302982) abstract confirms noninferiority and superiority.
efficacy.model: Juvenile hemophilia B dogs given the canine surrogate AAVRh74var-cFIX-R338L
efficacy.note: Surrogate-vector dogs had no bleeds for up to 547 days; BENEGENE-2 met its noninferiority ABR primary endpoint vs FIX prophylaxis.
efficacy.short: ABR noninferior to prophylaxis, as dogs predicted
efficacy.quote: The recommendation for approval is based on a demonstration of non-inferior annualized bleeding rate (ABR) compared to routine prophylaxis (RP) with exogenous FIX product administration
efficacy.reason: Fidanacogene ABR met, as filed dogs predicted
efficacy.judgement: Dog side from the same SBRA: 'No bleeds were observed in recipient animals.' The SBRA reports both but does not compare them, so comparison_stated false. Year from the NCT03861273 results posting (2024-03-27); an earlier sponsor topline release was not looked up.

patient_trials.quote: In the higher-dose cohort, mean FIX activity increased to 6.9 IU/dL.
One participant achieved sustained therapeutic FIX activity of ∼20%, without bleeding or replacement therapy, for 4 years; in others, FIX activity was not sustained beyond 5 to 11 weeks.
Sustained factor IX levels in the normal range were observed with low doses of FLT180a but necessitated immunosuppression with glucocorticoids with or without tacrolimus.

safety.population: Severe or moderately severe hemophilia B (FIX activity ≤2%)
safety.model: Hemophilia B dogs given liver-directed AAV8-canine FIX-Padua (R338L)
safety.note: FIX-Padua in dogs, even at ~200% activity, caused no thrombosis; mice showed wild-type immunogenicity and thrombogenicity.
safety.quote: Provocative studies in mice showed that FIX-Padua exhibits similar immunogenicity and thrombogenicity compared with FIX wild type.

safety.population: Severe or moderately severe hemophilia B (FIX activity ≤2%)
safety.confidence_note: Full text. Quote is a 34-word sentence fragment (sentence continues 'data have been limited...'); patient result: 'no development of factor IX inhibitors, no thrombosis'.
safety.model: Hemophilia B dogs given liver-directed AAV8-canine FIX-Padua (R338L)
safety.note: As in dogs, no patient developed a FIX inhibitor or thrombosis on sustained FIX-Padua expression.
safety.short: No inhibitor or thrombosis, as in dogs
safety.quote: Although the long-term expression of factor IX–R338L in canine models of hemophilia and preliminary data regarding short-term expression in a previous clinical trial did not show inhibitor formation or evidence of thrombosis
safety.reason: No inhibitor or thrombosis, as dogs showed
safety.judgement: Capsid-directed transaminase rises (2 of 10 here; 62% needing glucocorticoids in BENEGENE-2) are set aside as a harm the species could not show: George 2017 states 'the lack of animal models that recapitulate the human cellular immune response to the AAV capsid' and Konkle 2021 says the same. FDA's NHP toxicology (SBRA 2024) found no test-article findings at 2-10× the dose. Not scored: arteriovenous-fistula thrombosis in the FLT180a patient with 260% FIX (Chowdary 2022), whose preclinical model I could not read; BENEGENE-2 had no thrombotic events.

safety.population: Severe or moderately severe hemophilia B (FIX activity ≤2%)
safety.model: Hemophilia B dogs given subcutaneous dalcinonacog alfa
safety.note: Daily SC dalcinonacog alfa caused no adverse events or pro-coagulant laboratory abnormalities in hemophilia B dogs.
safety.quote: There were no treatment-emergent, clinically significant adverse events, and no abnormal hematology, chemistry, or pro-coagulant laboratory abnormalities throughout this study.

safety.population: Severe or moderately severe hemophilia B (FIX activity ≤2%)
safety.confidence_note: Full text both sides; transient early rises make the match partial.
safety.model: Hemophilia B dogs given subcutaneous dalcinonacog alfa
safety.note: Thrombogenicity markers in patients stayed normal or rose briefly then fell; no thrombotic event; ADA in 2, none neutralizing.
safety.short: No thrombogenicity signal, as in dogs
safety.quote: Thrombogenicity markers remained normal throughout prophylactic injections or showed some initial increases followed by decreases with continued dosing.
safety.reason: Thrombogenicity markers held, as dogs showed
safety.judgement: Paired by me. Anti-drug antibodies (2 non-neutralizing here; neutralizing in 2 Phase 1/2 patients, You 2021) are set aside: a human protein in dogs cannot predict human immunogenicity.
